## Summary

What problem does this change address, and what changed?

## Change type

- [ ] implementation / bug fix
- [ ] tests / validators
- [ ] machine contract / Manifest
- [ ] claim / evidence / transfer contract
- [ ] documentation / examples
- [ ] repository infrastructure / metadata
- [ ] maintenance / governance

## Affected surfaces

List the implementation, validators, `MANIFEST.yaml`, active contracts, examples, documentation, or public metadata affected. Note related surfaces intentionally left unchanged.

## Epistemic impact

Describe changes to claim/evidence structure, runtime policy, provenance, score semantics, assertion basis, conflicts, transfer, or reproducibility boundaries.

Keep structural state, source authority, evidence sufficiency, correctness, and scientific validity separate.

## Verification performed

List exact tests, validators, schema checks, provider fixtures, or other commands actually run and their observed results.

## Known limits / verification not performed

List relevant checks, provider routes, environments, external sources, or reproductions not exercised. Do not present contract inspection as execution evidence.

## Synchronization and historical impact

State which machine contracts, examples, explanatory docs, or metadata must remain synchronized. Preserve historical point-in-time evidence when a current-document correction is sufficient.

## Security and privacy

Describe provider, parser, source-data, external-tool, permission, or sensitive-data impact. Follow `SECURITY.md` for sensitive reports.

## Publication / metadata impact

State whether `CITATION.cff`, `codemeta.json`, `RELEASE_POLICY.md`, README, or other public discovery surfaces must remain synchronized.

## Rollback

Describe the smallest safe rollback.

## Review checklist

- [ ] The diff is limited to the stated purpose.
- [ ] Tests/checks described as passing were actually executed.
- [ ] Heuristic scores are not presented as calibrated probability.
- [ ] Claim transfer is not presented as acceptance or evidence sufficiency.
- [ ] Historical evidence was not silently rewritten to match later state.
- [ ] No credentials, private data, caches, or unrelated generated/local state is included.
